**Use
r testing, what visitors did**: the analytics reads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and s

ignals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studi
es/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm run
s |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before qu
oting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window, and where you get the `windowI
d` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies
/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending`
|\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `
409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Tak
es `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable
id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |\
n\nThe `usage` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `defe
rred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassign
ed`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nth
e map independently. Reading this response never starts analysis.\n\nTaxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery st
atus. Theme ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its the
me is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views w
ith version provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.\n\nCheck `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting cov
erage as a\nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's
displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather\nthan a fabri

cated map node.

The five analytics shapes above are **open objects** and gain fields over time.
Read what you recognize; ignor

e the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits**; the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on t
he same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights: one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read ra
ther\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is never inferred from anything el

se.

**Feedback**: report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /f
eedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, ope
ration?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only
(guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictly; an empty or o
ver-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goes to the MCPJam team, ou

tside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback
` MCP tool calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one;\n> it lets the team find that req
uest in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the original\n> recei

pt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning**: one read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| Endpoint | What it do
es |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, feature availability, plan limits, and the boo

leans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write still enforces
> its own ch
ecks, so a write can still fail with `403` after `capabilities`\n> reported `true`. Handle the write's own response rather than re

lying on this
> read alone.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCP

Jam/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Server accounts

A saved s
erver signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users\ncan't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password
and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nto a named account before each run.\

n
| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../accounts` | The accounts yo
u can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` |
One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`
, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: true`), or both |\n| `DELETE
.../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables
\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \
\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sen
sitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": { \"clientId\": \"'\"$CLIENT

iresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`{account}` is an a
ccount id or a name. A well-formed account id is always\nread as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to
an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account has makes `PUT` create the a

ccount; on every other route it
answers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.
\
nA name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and\nis at most 64 characters. One outside that rule,
or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are\nunique on the server, ignoring

case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and
 replacing a t
oken replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name\n for one test user.\n* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Host
ed runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner\n included. Asking for i
t is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body\n takes o
nly `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_tok

en` is
 refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.
* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**
* **A refresh tok
en is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refr
